text:
monitoring-bot: [ALERT] spike in model artifact fetch errors from Hugging Face registry. 429/504 observed from artifact fetcher (artifact-fetcher svc) for model 'redwood/gptx-small', error-rate ~18% over last 5m.

incident-bot: Paging @Devon SRE as on-call (severity P1 candidate). Incident channel: #incidents. Runbook: hf-artifact-rate-limit.

Devon SRE: Got the page. I'm looking at artifact-fetcher logs and the HF client metrics. Initial hypothesis: remote rate limits + our cold start prefetches creating thundering herd.

Alice M: Seeing customer-side errors in prod: a handful of active customers reporting elevated latency and some 502s when requests hit cold workers. Correlation with model fetch errors.

Ben K: Repro: run from a node: 
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "https://huggingface.co/api/models/redwood/gptx-small/weights" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN'
```
returns 429 too many requests intermittently. Response headers: `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `retry-after: 30` in several attempts.

Carmen (infra): Confirmed. Artifact proxy (artifact-cache) is showing backlog: cache-miss fetch latency spikes from 200ms -> 6s and some 504s. Our artifact-fetch concurrency appears to be ~200 concurrent prefetch workers after recent rollout.

Devon SRE: Immediate mitigations I'm doing now:
- Reduce artifact-fetcher concurrency to 20 (temp)
- Enable soft-fallback to cached quantized variant (gptx-small-q4) for in-flight requests
- Flip circuit-breaker to fail-fast for fetch errors to avoid blocking request threads

Devon SRE: Commands I'm running: 
```
# scale down prefetch workers
kubectl -n prod scale deploy artifact-fetcher --replicas=1
# tweak config
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/artifact-fetcher PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=20
```

Alice M: Noted. Pushing a temporary client fallback rule in routing to prefer existing warm workers and avoid triggering new cold starts.

Ben K: Adding a temporary header-based fallback for customers with active sessions to prefer cached model instances. Will push a small proxy rule.

Carmen (infra): Reached out to HF support (ticket 34122). They replied: "We're currently applying global rate-limiting due to high traffic; recommend using HF Hub mirrors or local caching. Retry-after provided." They gave no ETA.

Devon SRE: Status update: after scaling down concurrency and enabling fail-fast circuit, artifact-fetcher error-rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in 7 minutes. Cold start latency for new workers improved slightly because we stopped queuing fetches. Still seeing occasional 429s when cache-miss occurs.

Alice M: Customer impact summary for ops: ~2% of requests returning 502s at peak for ~30m across EU and us-east. Major customers with heavy cold-start patterns saw higher error rates; we sent a brief advisory to affected CSMs.

incident-bot: Handoff: @Devon SRE -> @Alice M for mitigation continuity. Devon remains on-call but Alice will coordinate cross-team fixes.

Ben K: Suggestion: spin up a temporary artifact CDN mirror in our infra pointing to an available S3-backed mirror we maintain for critical models. It will take ~20-30m to sync the hot revision. Is that acceptable?

Carmen (infra): We have last-known-good artifacts in internal blobstore for some models. I can trigger a prioritized background sync of gptx-small -> artifact-cache and serve from internal mirror. Doing that now.

Devon SRE: Also enabling a short-lived 'prefetch on write' warm-up for the most common model endpoints to mitigate further cold starts. This will be limited to 10 warm workers.

Alice M: Customer comms draft (sent to CSMs): "We're observing transient fetch errors from a third-party model hosting provider; our engineers have enacted fallbacks and are serving from cached variants while we mirror hot artifacts. We're monitoring and will update in 30 minutes."

Ben K: Telemetry note: adding a label 'hf-rate-limit' to all affected traces so we can filter prior/post mitigation.

monitoring-bot: Graphs: artifact-fetcher 5m error rate: 18% -> 6% after config change. Model cold-start lat p95 improved 18s -> 6.5s.

Carmen (infra): Internal mirror sync completed for gptx-small revision v2026-03-15-11. We now have a successful artifact-cache hit rate jump: cache-hit 78% -> 96% for that model.

Devon SRE: Rolling back the prefetch concurrency change gradually to 50 while watching HF headers for retry-after. If HF rate limits persist we keep low concurrency.

Alice M: Customer impact update: errors falling back to baseline. No new customer escalations in last 25m. Keeping incident open until HF confirms lifted or until our mirror prove stable for 2 hours.

Devon SRE: Postmortem action items (initial):
- Implement automatic artifact mirror fallback when HF returns 429s (owner: Carmen)
- Add dynamic prefetch throttling tied to upstream rate-limit headers (owner: Ben)
- Improve observability: surface HF rate-limit response headers in alerting (owner: Devon)
- Update runbook with circuit-breaker defaults for artifact fetches (owner: Alice)

incident-bot: Incident severity set to P2 (reduced) and incident notes updated.

Alice M: I'll schedule a post-incident review in #eng-runtime tomorrow 11:00am. Devon/Carmen/Ben please bring logs and timeline.

Devon SRE: Will capture a full timeline + logs and include HF response headers. Leaving the thread in monitoring watch.

monitoring-bot: Closing alert: artifact fetch error rate returned to baseline. Keeping incident thread open for postmortem.

Carmen (infra): FYI - HF replied to ticket 34122: "We experienced a short-lived rate limiting window due to a misconfigured autoscaler; mitigation applied. Please use mirrors for high-volume automated fetches."

Alice M: Thanks team. Adding final notes to incident tracker and tagging customers who saw impact.

(End of thread)
